content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is it possible to connect both [product_name] AM2 and [product_name] AM2 RTD directly to the [product_name] base module? The specifications mention 12...24V. Elsewhere, I've found notes suggesting these modules are used between 230V and 12/24V modules, which is a bit confusing. Best regards, [user_name]

Analog expansion modules can be directly connected to 230 VAC base or expansion modules. However, you need a separate 12 ... 24 VDC power supply for these modules. After analog modules, you can only connect further analog expansion modules or digital 12/24 VDC expansion modules—connecting 230 VAC expansion modules is not permitted. Refer to the attached [document] for more details.

Thank you for your response. I'll ensure to supply 12/24V. For my knowledge, why is it not allowed to connect further 230V modules after analog modules? Is there an electrical barrier or some kind of physical limitation? Best regards, [user_name]

The issue arises because the bus on 230 VAC devices is not electrically isolated from the supply voltage. Analog modules have bus galvanic isolation at their input but not at their output. Base modules and digital expansion modules lack bus isolation entirely.

analysis.insight_summary: A user asked about connecting specific analog expansion modules to the base module and noted unclear documentation about voltage compatibility and connection sequence. The discussion clarified that direct connection is possible, but separation of power supply and understanding of electrical isolation are essential to avoid system issues. Documentation inconsistencies, particularly concerning the prohibition of chaining 230V modules after analog ones, are a source of uncertainty.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking clearer documentation describing the correct way to connect expansion modules of varying voltage types, with explicit reasons for any technical restrictions to support safe installations.
